First release of keydrift.

After a supply chain or platform incident, keydrift tells you which of your keys it touched. It reads the places where API keys end up on a developer machine (AI agent logs, shell histories, env files, tool configs and CI files), lists every key it finds without ever showing the value, and gives you a rotation list with the most urgent key first and a link to the page where you revoke it.

- `keydrift scan` lists keys, credential files and CI secret names, plus the rotation list.
- `keydrift snapshot` and `keydrift diff` save a fingerprint-only snapshot and later show new keys and keys that moved to a new place.
- `keydrift match` checks the machine for signs of a known incident. This release knows litellm 1.107.0, the OVHcloud CLI swap, and the Railway, Zeabur and OpenCode incidents from October 2026.

It only reads files. It never runs anything it finds, never calls a provider and sends nothing over the network.

Binaries below are static builds for Linux and macOS (amd64 and arm64). Check them against checksums.txt.
